reasons: The PromQL multiplies the result by a constant 100 that does not appear in the Datadog source (avg:postgresql.rows_returned{$scope}, no formula scaling). Hard rules forbid unsourced numeric constants, so the scale must be dropped; any unit-scale concern belongs in notes only.

Without the 100 factor, avg(rate(postgresql.tup_returned[$__rate_interval])) is a reasonable match: tup_returned is a monotonic sum, so rate() is allowed, and the per-second rate matches the widget's 'per sec' title.
The $scope template variable has no prefix and default '*', so dropping it is correct.
Grouping and series are unchanged (no by-clause, avg across all series), so those aspects match.
